theme: Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
queries_run: gh search repos "common crawl web graph rank"
gh search repos "tranco top sites list"
gh search repos "common crawl host graph"
gh search repos "ai crawler traffic dataset"
gh search repos "gtab anchored google trends"

candidates.name: cloudflare-radar-rankings-cache
candidates.what_it_holds: Automated daily/weekly mirror of Cloudflare Radar's domain popularity rankings, committed as gzip-compressed CSVs at four tiers (top-1k, top-10k, top-100k, top-1m), one 'domain' column per file, unordered (membership-only, not rank-ordered). Stored both as dated snapshots (YYYY-MM-DD dirs, so a time series builds up) and a current/ pointer. MIT-licensed code, data itself under Cloudflare Radar terms. Actively updated (commit within the last day as of scrape).
candidates.why_useful: Gives a longitudinal, point-in-time-able snapshot of which domains are in Cloudflare's top-N popularity tiers each day/week — the closest free proxy to a Similarweb-style traffic-rank history for airbnb.com and competitor domains (booking.com, vrbo.com, expedia.com). Speaks to gap 5 (engagement/web-traffic estimates) and could be checked for airbnb.com's tier membership over time as a crude traffic-trend indicator, with the caveat that it's membership not rank-value.
candidates.time_coverage: ongoing snapshots, apparently started 2026; check earliest commit for history depth
candidates.size_hint: 4 gzip CSVs per snapshot day, up to 1M rows in the largest tier

candidates.name: cloudflare-bot-directory
candidates.what_it_holds: Single committed JSON file (src/index.json) listing 500+ verified crawlers/bots from Cloudflare Radar's Verified Bots directory, with fields slug, name, kind, operator, operatorUrl, category, description, followsRobotsTxt, userAgentPatterns, userAgents. This is a static snapshot, not a traffic-share time series.
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-theme for gap 19 (AI-referral traffic / bot crawler share) as a reference table of which bots exist and how to identify them in logs, but it holds no traffic volume or share data itself — only bot identity metadata. Useful mainly as a lookup table if we ever get log-level crawler-traffic data from elsewhere.
candidates.license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (data), repo code license unspecified

candidates.name: cc-webgraph
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Common Crawl Java toolkit to build host-level and domain-level web graphs from Common Crawl crawl data and compute PageRank / Harmonic Centrality rankings using the WebGraph framework. No graph files or ranking CSVs are committed in the repo itself — the actual host-rank datasets (domain harmonic-centrality and PageRank tables, updated with most Common Crawl monthly crawls) are announced/hosted separately on commoncrawl.org's webgraph release pages (e.g. s3://commoncrawl/projects/hyperlinkgraph/).
candidates.why_useful: This is the authoritative method for producing a Common Crawl-derived domain popularity/authority rank for airbnb.com and competitor domains over time (each crawl release gives a new rank snapshot, several times a year back to 2017) — a genuine point-in-time web-authority series, complementary to our existing Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com pages. Falls under gap 5 (web-traffic-like popularity proxies) as an acquisition method rather than a stored dataset; the actual rank tables must be pulled from Common Crawl's S3 announcements, which are public and free.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 (repo); data on commoncrawl.org is public domain / CC0-like per Common Crawl's terms
candidates.time_coverage: Common Crawl webgraph releases exist for multiple crawls per year, historically back to ~2017
candidates.size_hint: graph files are large (multi-GB); ranking tables per crawl cover hundreds of millions of hosts/domains
candidates.last_activity: actively maintained by Common Crawl Foundation
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Extends what we hold (Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com, 2.08M rows) with an actual domain-rank/authority metric rather than just a page index

candidates.name: radar-rs
candidates.what_it_holds: Unofficial Rust SDK/client wrapper for the Cloudflare Radar API (BGP routing stats, attack data, DNS, HTTP traffic metrics, bot-traffic breakdowns, top ASNs). Read-only client, requires the user's own Cloudflare API token; commits no data itself.
candidates.why_useful: Lower-friction way to pull Cloudflare Radar's HTTP-traffic-by-category and bot/crawler-traffic-share endpoints (which include an internet-traffic-by-industry breakdown covering 'Internet & Telecom'/travel-adjacent categories and AI-bot vs human traffic share) programmatically, relevant to gap 19 (AI-referral / bot crawler share). Requires a free Cloudflare account/API token (not a paid key), so within the 'no paid API keys' rule, but is a thin client rather than a dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: live API, no historical bulk export

candidates.name: ai-visibility-readiness
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source 'AI Visibility Readiness' audit methodology: deterministic HTTP/HTML probes plus live citation measurement, with Cloudflare Radar crawler baselines used to benchmark how much of a site's traffic is AI-bot crawlers vs human. Auto-generates a CHECKS.md from the audit code; framework, not a pre-collected panel.
candidates.why_useful: A candidate method (not data) for measuring how 'AI-crawlable'/AI-referenced a given site is, tying to gap 19's LLM-travel-agent-benchmark angle — could in principle be pointed at airbnb.com or competitor booking sites to get an AI-crawler-traffic baseline, though this would count as scraping and needs a human ToS call per repo rules.

candidates.name: domain-industry-enricher
candidates.what_it_holds: Small DIY tool that enriches a list of top domains with industry/category classification using the Cloudflare Radar API (categorizes domains, e.g. travel, e-commerce). No committed dataset, requires a Cloudflare API token.
candidates.why_useful: Could be paired with the cloudflare-radar-rankings-cache top-domain lists to isolate travel/OTA-category domains and track their tier membership over time as a competitor-visibility proxy, but is purely a small utility script with no data of its own.

candidates.name: partially.online
candidates.what_it_holds: Real-time internet outage/restriction dashboard aggregating live data from IODA, OONI, and Cloudflare Radar; trinocular Bayesian probing, severity scoring, 30-day country timelines. Not travel/search specific but demonstrates a working multi-source Radar aggregation pipeline.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: could be adapted to flag country-level internet disruptions (which would depress both search demand and STR bookings in a market) as an event/shock indicator, but this is a stretch use of an outage-monitoring tool rather than a direct search/SEO dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: rolling 30-day live window, no long history committed

notes: This theme is thin on GitHub: keyword-volume tools (Bing/Google Keyword Planner clones), true backlink datasets, and Tranco-list mirrors returned zero hits via gh search repos with plain-text queries (Tranco itself is typically obtained via tranco-list.eu's own API/site, not a GitHub mirror repo of the ranking CSV; consider a scout retrying with `--topic=` filters or `gh search code` — which we did not use, staying under the 10/min cap). SERP-scraper searches surfaced only generic paid-API tutorial repos (Oxylabs, HasData, ScraperAPI comparison spam) with no committed data and mostly no Airbnb/travel relevance — excluded as boilerplate per instructions. Common Crawl's actual webgraph/host-rank datasets live on commoncrawl.org's S3 buckets, not in a GitHub-hosted dataset repo; cc-webgraph is the tool to build/consume them and is the most substantive method-based finding for this theme. AI-crawler-traffic-share data (Cloudflare Radar's public dashboards do publish an aggregate 'AI bot traffic' metric) has no dedicated GitHub dataset repo found; only client libraries and audit tools exist. WebSearch quota was exhausted mid-task (shared session budget across other concurrent scouts), so this scout relied on gh search repos plus WebFetch of individual repo READMEs; a rerun with WebSearch available could probably find more (e.g. GDELT-adjacent SEO/backlink corpora, or academic replication packages using Common Crawl's Web Data Commons hyperlink graph, which is a strong existing target at https://webdatacommons.org but is not itself a GitHub repo).
cost_note: gh search repos calls used: 8 (over the nominal 6-call guidance because early single-term queries returned empty and were re-tried with related terms; no gh search code calls were made).
